proposed behavior: P82 as written, built for one agency first: domestic violence is the victims of murder and nonnegligent manslaughter (09A), negligent manslaughter (09B), the sex offenses (11A-11D), the assaults (13A-13C), kidnapping (100), incest and statutory rape (36A, 36B) and human trafficking (64A, 64B) whose incident has an offense segment with that code and where any offender of the incident is the victim's intimate partner (SE CS BG XS XR HR) or family or household member (CH PA SB OF SC SP GP GC IL CF BE SS FP FC CO), each victim counted once. "Intimate partner violence" and "IPV" are domestic violence by intimate partners; "family violence" is domestic violence by family members. The answer carries one plain note defining it. Domestic violence incidents are the distinct incidents with at least one such victim, said in one more sentence. Domestic violence offenses are the offenses of those crimes in incidents that had a domestic violence victim, and domestic violence arrests are the people arrested on such incidents (the data does not link an arrest to the victim), each said in one more sentence. A state, the nation or several places are declined until built and timed. Murders and negligent manslaughter among them are not answered here: "domestic violence murders" and "domestic homicides" come from Homicide Reports (P169, Jeff 2026-11-22).
exact default or choices offered: The victims count (by year or month), the one-sentence definition, one agency.
